title: Revise defaults-loop design: apply review 1, add introspection step
summary: Revise docs/design/defaults-loop.md to apply every change in review 1 and add introspection as a first-class step, using the operator's cases as reported evidence. Per the user's reply, the design must say which part of Athena reads past records (code outside the agent snapshot or a filtered view) and what it passes on. Design only.

defaults_applied.how: Revision is a written design with alternatives (records reader choice, fallback choice).
Operator cases labelled reported; numbers measured or labelled estimates.
One document revision plus its decision-log and changelog entries; no code.
Job ids only; no personal data.
Introspection design targets causes beyond the instance.

assumptions: The review file lists seven changes (F1-F5, two Medium, Lows) as in the earlier reading; I did not re-read it.
D90 in docs/decisions.md must be edited to stay consistent with the F1 change.
Records are read by Athena code outside the agent snapshot, which hands the introspecting agent only a filtered summary; this is the stated assumption the doc will justify.
Design only: no code for introspection is written.

acceptance_criteria.text: defaults-loop.md restates Jev's role so Jev only answers typed questions (cluster assignment or pairwise boolean) and a language model drafts statement, applies_to and title; D90 in docs/decisions.md matches (F1).

Section 2 labels the R2 reader-budget overrun as a counter-example, states R1 is closed in code by D89, marks the loop's case as unproved, and gates any build on at least N distinct jobs a default would cover (F2).

A section documents POST /v1/evaluate: request fields (model, state, questions with type, instructions, criteria), response fields (choice, probabilities, confidence), chat-route refusal as a build error, fake Jev following that shape, cost/tokens read from the response (F4).
Top-probability and confidence signals are defined with what each controls, fallback vs explicit second call is chosen, and the answering model is stored in evidence (F5).

Reader budget is stated by first sentence plus id/scope and entry count, says where the full statement lands, defines the intervention record as the single counted unit, and makes a render() measurement with the live counter a gate on the 1,500-token estimate.

Promotion criterion computes the test-part size needed for a skill lower bound or drops the interval for user judgment (F3); D26 'eleven' and the RM-3 citation are corrected; Low items from the review are done.

Introspection is a first-class step: triggered by every correction, intervention, rejection and failure, run and recorded by Athena, with fields what happened, failure class and earlier cases, cause beyond the instance, prevention (default, code check or design change), proposed next request; retries start from the record; the defaults loop consumes records; class matching is a typed /v1/evaluate decision for Jev.

The design states which part of Athena reads past records/ (code outside the agent snapshot, or a filtered view given to the introspecting agent), picks one, and says exactly what it passes on to the agent and onward.

The operator's cases (8qkc/m1bs CHANGELOG; 69gf/t1y6/3p3y/jk8v reader budget; #47 checks not finished; 69gf Haiku untested; 16zf BRIEF.md edit; design+build bundling; Jev interface assumed) are each labelled reported, with class and what would have prevented it.
No Rust, config, defaults.toml, BRIEF.md, records/ or review file changes; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only markdown files under docs/ and CHANGELOG.md changed; `cargo test` still passes.

out_of_scope: Any Rust code or tests for introspection
Edits to BRIEF.md, defaults.toml, athena.toml, records/ or the review file
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than reference: a large two-part doc revision with many checkable content criteria.
